label: Where a limb stops, it writes (levitation)
notes: One limb's trail through a dance is one contiguous line (black); wherever that limb holds still, the line leaves its path and draws, small, what the other limbs did during the hold, seen from the stopped limb, then closes back onto the stop and goes on. The second limb (red) does the same on the same surface. Each sign is different and none is invented: the signs went from a vocabulary (round 7) to a record. Levitation: the left hand in black, the left foot in red; the foot's stand becomes one large red figure. Ian, round 12: "love this". Keep makes a group: one layer per ink, each on its own pen. Controls: the dance, the two limbs (the second may be none, or all the others), how many seconds of the dance, how many figures per limb, how much more happening makes a figure larger, the seed (it only feeds the nib passes). The round-7 tree Ian saw beside it ("together they're almost a piece") is not offered: it is old experiment code (signs_study) and a fitted grammar, not a kit recipe. Frame 240 × 180 landscape: levitation's content is wide. (Bench v3, 2026-10-19: no seed control. The drawing is the recorded dance itself, read the same way every time; nothing in it is drawn at random, so a seed changed nothing.)
